SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - NOT REAL FDA GUIDANCE

U.S. Food and Drug Administration
Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER)
Draft Guidance for Industry
Title: Nitrosamine Impurity Control in Oral Solid Dosage Forms (Fictional Revision 4)
Issued: March 3, 2026

This draft guidance describes updated expectations for manufacturers of oral solid dosage forms regarding the assessment and control of N-nitrosamine impurities. Manufacturers must complete a risk assessment for all marketed products containing secondary or tertiary amine functional groups within 9 months of the final guidance publication. Where risk is identified, confirmatory testing using a validated, sufficiently sensitive method is required. The acceptable intake (AI) limit for any newly identified nitrosamine drug substance-related impurity (NDSRI) without compound-specific data defaults to 26.5 ng/day. Changes to manufacturing processes undertaken to mitigate nitrosamine formation must be reported in a Prior Approval Supplement (PAS) or Changes Being Effected in 30 days (CBE-30) as appropriate. Applicants should submit a summary of their risk assessment in their next annual report. Comments on this draft should be submitted within 60 days.

key_requirements: Complete nitrosamine risk assessment for amine-containing oral solid products within 9 months of final guidance
Perform confirmatory testing with a validated sensitive method where risk is identified
Apply default acceptable intake of 26.5 ng/day for NDSRIs without compound-specific data
Report mitigating manufacturing changes via PAS or CBE-30
Summarize risk assessment in next annual report
output.summary: Draft FDA guidance tightening nitrosamine impurity risk assessment, testing, and acceptable intake limits for oral solid dosage forms.
